title: Operational Initiative Tracker: SLO Ownership Rotations & Error-Budget Playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Create an operational initiative tracker and accompanying playbook that codifies SLO ownership rotations, error-budget policies, and quick remediation guidance so product, platform, and on-call teams can reliably manage reliability objectives without ad-hoc coordination.

Scope:
- Define a lightweight cadence for SLO stewardship (weekly on-call rotation + monthly steward review).
- Produce an Error-Budget Playbook with concrete runbooks for common burn patterns (traffic spike, regression, infra failure, model quality drift).
- Build a minimal initiative tracker (dashboard + lifecycle states) integrated with Console alerts and PagerDuty/Slack so ownership handoffs are visible.
- Surface specific SLI definitions for core inference paths (request success rate, p95 latency, p99 latency, model-reply correctness signal).
- Document escalation and rollback criteria tied to error-budget spend thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook published in Confluence with page links referenced in the ticket and a one-pager summary added to the Engineering onboarding folder.
2) Tracker table in Console that lists active SLO initiatives, current owner, rotation schedule, error-budget remaining, and last mitigation action.
3) Automated alert rules: 3 tiers (informational at 25% burn, owner ack + mitigation suggestions at 50%, org escalation at 75% and automated soft-fallback at 90%).
4) Two runbooks (traffic spike and model-quality regression) tested via a tabletop exercise with site reliability and ML infra teams and an incident playbook review completed.
5) Handoff pattern documented and validated with at least 3 stewards across product and platform.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Ownership cadence: weekly rotation chosen to minimize steward fatigue while keeping attention frequent enough to catch early burns. Monthly steward review remains for cross-initiative alignment.
- Alert thresholds: conservative thresholds reduce noisy escalations but may admit higher burn before action; stakeholders preferred earlier soft notifications to gather telemetry context.
- Tracker surface: we will avoid a monolithic new app. Start with a Console-integrated table + a simple Google Sheet sync for non-console consumers to minimize engineering lift.

Milestones:
- Week 1 (2025-01-13 to 2025-01-17): Author playbook skeleton, define SLI set and thresholds.
- Week 2: Build Console tracker prototype and wire basic alerts.
- Week 3: Run tabletop and iterate runbooks.
- Week 4: Publish playbook, switch rotation schedule live, and collect feedback from first steward rotation.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Alert fatigue from overly aggressive thresholds. Mitigation: start with a 25% informational threshold, instrument snooze/annotations and capture signal-to-noise in first two rotations.
- Risk: Confusion about ownership across Dedicated vs Hosted products. Mitigation: include product-surface tags and a migration checklist in playbook.
